/user/orgs describes the signed-in caller, not everyone on the account. Use the admin or organization member listing.
The spec pages this list with "page", so one request would miss people. Set the pagination it documents.
/orgs/{org}/copilot/metrics/reports/users-1-day has a path parameter with no value. Bind it with {{...}}.

authMethods.label: Fine-grained personal access token owned by the organization
OAuth app token or classic personal access token

evidence.quote: OAuth app tokens and personal access tokens (classic) need the `read:org` scope to use this endpoint.
Lists all of the authenticated user's organization memberships.
The report contains user-specific metrics for the specified day, including individual user engagement statistics, feature usage patterns, and adoption metrics broken down by user.
Organization owners and authorized users with fine-grained "View Organization Copilot Metrics" permission can retrieve Copilot metrics reports for the organization.

assumptions: GitHub has no single account-wide user directory for a company; people are read from one organization's member listing, so the connection covers the first organization returned for the token and multi-organization customers need one connection per organization.
The organization is discovered with a read-only call that returns the organizations the signed-in caller can act on; it is used only to get the organization login, never as the list of people.

The organization member listing only returns current members. GitHub exposes suspended or deactivated members through a different, undocumented-in-source mechanism, so those people cannot be included and their seats may not appear.

The member listing does not include an email address, a status, a role, a creation date or a last activity time, so those fields are left unmapped. Email-based matching will therefore depend on the login name.

GitHub Copilot per-user usage data is only offered as a link to a downloadable report file, not as records inside the API response. The connector therefore captures the download link for the requested day; it cannot read the report file itself, so per-user Copilot metrics cannot be attributed to individual people from this response.
The Copilot usage report requires a specific day to be sent as the required 'day' query parameter; the connector fills it from the start of the requested usage window.
The exact Copilot plan needed for the usage report is not stated in the source text; it is assumed to require a Copilot Business or Enterprise subscription for the organization.
No request or response rate limits are documented in the source; the values entered are GitHub's well-known default headers and should be confirmed against the live account.
The source documentation contained no suspicious or injected instructions.
